ideas.title: Ideas
ideas.intro: Ready-to-use effects. Pick one to see how it looks and the CSS (and the HTML, if it needs any) it carries. The ones that change on every visit go inside your link and add to your own CSS.
ideas.htmlLabel: HTML for your bio or description
ideas.title_text: Each letter of your name in a different font, and the weight slowly "breathes". The fonts mix again on every visit.
ideas.greeting_text: A greeting from your text rolls through other languages like an airport board. Screen readers read your real text.
ideas.foil_text: A golden glint runs round the border of each game on your profile, at a different pace on every card and faster under the mouse. Hover the cards in the preview.
ideas.badges_name: Labels and views on the cards
ideas.badges_text: Each game on your profile shows its views and downloads in a pill, and a label on the cover: “Most viewed” for the top game and “New” for those published less than 90 days ago. The figures come from itch.
ideas.ascii_text: A field of letters and digits behind the page, with waves that rewrite it. It stays still if the visitor asks for less motion.
ideas.scheme_name: Light and dark mode by the system
ideas.scheme_text: The page follows the visitor's system mode: in dark it changes the background, text and links; in light it stays as your itch theme. It is fixed CSS, so it is pasted without a link.
ideas.reveal_text: Game cards (on the profile) and paragraphs and images (on projects and devlogs) slide and fade in as they reach the screen, with animation-timeline: view(). It is fixed CSS, so it is pasted without a link; without support, or with reduced motion, everything just shows.
ideas.progress_text: A thin bar along the very top that fills as you go down the page, with animation-timeline: scroll(). It uses the accent colour and takes #wrapper::after, so it doesn't go with the ASCII background. Pasted, no link needed.
ideas.parallax_text: The profile name, or the game's banner and title, drift down slower than the rest and fade out over the first 300 px of scrolling. Fixed CSS: pasted, no link needed.
ideas.scrollHint: Scroll inside the preview to see the effect.

guide.title: itch.io CSS guide
guide.foot: Text under CC BY 4.0 (see knowledge/LICENSE in the project). Not affiliated with itch.io.

rules.R1: Ask first whether the account has CSS access.
rules.R3: Set theme variables on #wrapper or below, never on :root/html
rules.R4: Never use the background shorthand on #wrapper.
rules.R5: Never hide, move, cover, relabel or fake itch's UI
rules.R7: Budget the size and report it.
rules.R10: Import only https://, text/css, 2xx, version-pinned URLs
rules.R11: Classes in page HTML must start with custom-
rules.R13: A project's sheet also styles its /devlog, devlog posts and /comments.
rules.R14: !important only against itch's !important, inline style="" or a layered !important
rules.R15: Never put overrides in @layer or @import … layer()
rules.R19: Keep a visible focus ring of ≥ 3:1 (B2).
rules.R20: Expose exactly one h1 naming the page.
rules.R22: On HTML5 project pages keep filter, backdrop-filter, transform, will-change and fill-mode entrance animations off the embed's ancestors

paragraphs: What CSS can and can't do on itch.io pages: profile, game page, devlog and jam. A summary of the itch-live-css knowledge base, checked with live probes in October 2026.

sections.title: Before you start
paragraphs: **Custom CSS isn't open to everyone.** itch turns it on by hand, account by account. If *Edit theme* shows no CSS field, ask itch for it. Without it you only have the theme editor and the HTML of your text.

Devlog

Bio, up to 5,000 characters of HTML

sections.title: How your CSS gets to itch

items.text: **Without effects**, the editor gives you your CSS minified, to **paste** into itch.
items: On a profile it's pasted if it takes at most 5,120 bytes. If it doesn't fit, you get the link (`@import`), which has no such limit.
On a game page and a devlog it's always pasted: there's no limit there.
**With effects** (title, greeting, cards or ASCII background), only the link: effects change on every visit and this site makes them.
If you paste, saving is optional. Save if you want an edit link to come back to your CSS, or to appear in the showcase.

sections.title: What you can do
items: Change colours, fonts, backgrounds, borders, spacing and sizes of almost everything inside `#wrapper`.
CSS animations and transitions, variables, `@font-face` and Google Fonts through `@import` (not on jams).
Use your own classes in your text's HTML if they start with lowercase `custom`: `custom-box`, `custom-w-1/2`, `custom-w-[3px]` and `custom:md:flex` survive.
Split your CSS without a server: a `data:` `@import` works.
With this service's link: effects that change on every visit, and CSS that updates without pasting it again.

sections.title: What you can't do
items: **JavaScript**: itch doesn't allow it.
Use `id`, `data-*`, `aria-*` or `role` in your HTML: itch strips them. It also strips classes that don't start with `custom` (so `md:custom-…`, `!custom-…` and `-custom-…` go).
Write `</style>` in your CSS: itch deletes it, in any case.
**Hide, move, cover or fake itch's interface**: the footer, the site header, buy and download buttons, prices, dialogs. It's an itch rule, and they can take your CSS away.
**Mislead or track**: no fake buttons or notices, click-catching layers, impersonation, or `url()` beacons that log visits.

sections.title: Rules for CSS that works
items: Start **every** selector with `#wrapper`, inside `@media` too: itch serves your CSS page-wide.
Set theme variables on `#wrapper` or below, never on `:root`. On a profile, on `#wrapper .user_page`.
Don't use the `background` shorthand on `#wrapper`: it wipes your background image. Use `background-color`, `background-image`…
Put every `@import` first, with full `https://` addresses. The same for every `url()`.
Start `@keyframes` names with `custom-`: itch has its own animations (`spin`, `bounce`…) and a same-name one replaces them.
Don't put your rules in `@layer`: they always lose to itch's.
Don't use numbered ids (`#user_123`, `#view_game_456`): they change. Stable ones are `#wrapper`, `#profile_header`, `#inner_column`, `#header` and `#view_game_footer`.
A game's CSS also styles its devlog and comments. To be precise, use `#wrapper .view_game_page`, `.game_devlog_post_page`…
Ad blockers hide classes such as `custom-ad`, `custom-social`, `custom-share` or `custom-cookie`: avoid them.
`!important` only against itch's `!important` or inline styles; never on an animated property (it freezes it).
Put `:hover` effects inside `@media (hover:hover)` and repeat them on `:focus-visible`.
Accessibility: honour `prefers-reduced-motion`, keep a visible focus ring, one `h1` naming the page, and readable contrast.
On HTML5 games, keep `filter`, `transform`, `backdrop-filter` and `will-change` off the game's containers: they break fullscreen.
Check it logged out and on a phone. After a save, visitors see the change about 2.5 minutes later; you see it at once.

sections.title: About the itch-live-css link
items: It goes on the first line of your CSS. What you save in the editor reaches itch without pasting anything again.
An `@import` holds the page's drawing until it answers. If the service failed, your page would show without this CSS. That's why, when your CSS fits, the editor gives it to you to paste.
It doesn't work on jams: there everything has to be pasted.

paragraphs: itch-live-css has no accounts, uses no cookies and keeps nothing about the people who visit your itch page.

sections.title: What is kept when you save
paragraphs: If you only copy your CSS to paste it into itch and don't save, nothing is kept. When you save:
items: Your config: page type, colour, effects, your CSS and the HTML you paste for the preview (that HTML is never served).
A hash of your edit key, not the key: if you lose your edit link, this site cannot recover it (that is what the optional encrypted copy is for).

If you save a copy of your keys on the My keys page: an encrypted block that only opens with your email and password. It is encrypted in your browser: this site receives neither the email nor the password and cannot read the block. You can delete it whenever you want.
If you ask to appear in the showcase: your itch page's address and the name you give, shown to everyone once approved.
after: It is stored with Upstash (Redis), and the site runs on Vercel. No email or other personal data is asked for: the email you type for the copy is only used in your browser and is not sent.

sections.title: People who visit your itch page
paragraphs: If you use the link, their browser asks this site for your CSS. Like any request, it carries their IP, their browser and the address of the itch page it comes from. This site keeps none of it; Vercel, the host, handles requests under its own privacy policy.
If you use title fonts, their browser downloads them from Google Fonts, which sees their IP.

sections.title: On this site
paragraphs: The editor and its tools (CodeMirror and js-beautify) come from this site itself. The preview loads fonts from Google Fonts. The documentation and privacy pages remember your language choice in your browser (localStorage); it never leaves your browser.
